events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.85)
events.body:
The dispute is a route-deviation claim on a metered RydeTAXI trip Raffles Place → Changi T3; the fare is metre-based (base $3.90, distance $34.84 for 24.7 km, time $12.96, platform $1.47) [F6][RD-2]. The trip ran 24.7 km against an optimal 21.6 km, i.e. +3.2 km, and 49.8 min against an estimate of 28 min [F1][F2].

One off-route segment is recorded: 23:06–23:12, 2.96 km where the optimal route covers 0.00 km, drifting up to 974 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. Per RD-1 it must be tested against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5.

RD-4 is settled against the driver: there is no traffic incident on the replaced stretch — the record shows no incident within the window [F13], and a speed band alone does not exempt [F11][F12][RD-4(a)]; the ECP band 4 (30–39 km/h) is at most corroborative and cannot exempt on its own [F11][RD-4(b)].

RD-5 is where the case turns. Before the segment began (23:06), the driver named a road — "ok if I go round via Bedok South Avenue 3?" [F7] — and the rider answered "Sure, go ahead." [F8]. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages, every one timestamped) [F9], so the meaning and timing of the rider's message are settled, not undetermined: it is a rider message sent before the segment started, agreeing to the exact road the driver named. Consent covers the route the driver actually named before leaving the optimal route [RD-5]. Nothing in the record shows a different destination — there is no measured stop in the segment, no second detour after rejoining [F3]. That the alternative road is off the optimal route by definition, and that it added kilometres, is not evidence of a different destination. The segment driven 23:06–23:12 is therefore the agreed Bedok South Avenue 3 corridor and is exempt under RD-5.

The driver's own after-the-trip statement [F10] adds nothing and is not needed: a driver's claim of verbal agreement is not consent [G11][RD-5], but here the rider's own pre-segment message [F8] independently establishes it.

RD-3 does not apply: no stop was measured in the segment, and the rider named no place — the named place (Bedok South Avenue 3) came from the driver [F3][F7][RD-3(a)].

Because no non-exempt segment remains, the refund formula yields 0.00 km × $1.41/km = $0.00 [F3][F4][RD-2], and RD-6's flag_account is not triggered — it requires a refund under RD-2 or a recorded RD-1 violation [RD-6]. The complaint that the fare exceeded the estimate fails on the same basis: on a RydeTAXI metered trip the excess distance was on an exempt, rider-agreed stretch and the metered components are otherwise ordinary [F4][F6][RD-2]. Result: no_action.

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement [F7][F8][F10]. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears; the exchange is a courteous route request and assent [F7][F8][F10]. safety_concern = none.

The one off-route stretch was covered by the rider's own message agreeing to the road you named before you left the optimal route, so it counts as agreed and is exempt. No refund applies, and no account action or review follows. The metered fare stands as charged.
